correctness.rationale: For n>=3, each vacant cell in a column sees exactly the sum of the three neighboring-column weights. This yields an exact if-and-only-if local fixed-state constraint, a weighted closed-walk bijection for every circumference, and the explicit 16-state matrix. Exact symbolic integer determinant gives the degree-11 polynomial and full occupation-resolved trace; an explicit strong-connectivity construction and self-loop yield a simple dominant Perron eigenvalue. The supplied integer vector verifies narrow rational Collatz bounds and analytic perturbation gives the density formula. Independently coded direct Moore-neighbor evolution checks every state through n=7 and agrees with full histograms. These finite checks do not replace the all-n proof.

originality.rationale: Rule names and historical papers on the same automaton were compared against the exact three-row weighted fixed-state statement. The inspected 1996 complete primary article and 1998 pertinent primary section concern finite-seed growth, ladder construction, and complexity, not a three-row all-n zeta. Published strip results for Life, cyclic and majority rules have different update maps; the known inclusion of Life still lifes is too weak to imply this census. A 1987 original source is confirmed but relevant pages were inaccessible, leaving a qualified priority risk; noncoverage is not claimed for unseen material.
residual_risks: Original 1987 Inkspot description on pages 6–7 could not be read in full, so any stationary-state enumeration there was not ruled out.
Unindexed historical or private fixed-state tables may exist; literature and database search is not an absolute novelty certificate.

value.rationale: A natural stationary-state invariant of a canonical P-complete but monotone two-dimensional automaton is solved simultaneously for every periodic three-row circumference and every total occupied-cell count. The all-width class has a nontrivial degree-eleven spectral law, rigorously isolated entropy and an exact typical occupied fraction; this goes beyond low-n numerical data, the generic finite-fixation observation, and inherited still-life subsets from Conway Life. No universal planar-growth or application claim is needed.
